title: Ibn Battuta in Mali
hookLine: clean white clothes, mats sent ahead, and the Qur'an learned by heart (Rihla)
tomorrow: what goes in a pilgrim's journal the day he reaches Mecca?

cards: Fridays have a feeling: the week loosening, plans for the weekend. Ibn Battuta's Friday in Mali had a color: white.
People came to the mosque in clean white clothes, and if you didn't come early, he says, you'd find no place to pray at all, the crowd was so great.

teach.b: In the Rihla he lists what he admired in the people of Mali, and their care for prayer is among them. People sent servants ahead with prayer mats to hold their places.
Someone who owned a single shirt would wash it for Friday. And they were keen to learn the Qur'an by heart. He's not writing a brochure; in the same pages he criticizes customs he disliked.
The Qur'an names the day, in Pickthall: “O ye who believe! When the call is heard for the prayer of the day of congregation, haste unto remembrance of Allah and leave your trading.”
Now the debate, because Ibn Battuta was a traveler. Does Friday bind someone on the road?

One voice, from the books of law: a traveler is excused from the Friday prayer and prays the ordinary noon prayer instead. The road is hard, and the law was made with mercy; using that mercy is no failure.
Another voice, from teachers and travelers: if a mosque is near, go anyway. The excuse is a door left open, not a reason to miss the gathering, and a stranger in town is exactly who needs one.
Both sides honor Friday. One protects the traveler; the other protects the gathering. In Mali, Ibn Battuta went, and wrote down the white.

how: Muslims prepare for the Friday prayer by bathing, wearing clean clothes and coming early to the mosque; jurists excuse a traveler from it, and many travelers attend when a mosque is near.

clean white garments for the day of congregation.

games.q: your cousin, on a work trip, says the traveler's excuse means she'll skip Friday prayer. you lean toward going anyway. give her side's best case.
o: the law lightens the road on purpose; using a mercy isn't a failure.
Friday prayer is only meant for people who live near a mosque.
she doesn't need to go, since nobody would ever know.
games.why: the excuse is part of the law, made with the traveler's hardship in mind. the other side answers: if it's near, the gathering is still a gift. both honor Friday.

practice: Find something clean made of cloth: a shirt, a towel, a scarf. Hold it close and breathe in once, slowly, then lay it flat and smooth it with your palm.
Keep a hand resting on it for the rest of the sit, the way you'd ready clothes for a day you mean to honor.
